verses.sanskrit:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच।
              एवमेतन्महाबाहो रामेणामिततेजसा। प्राप्तं व्यसनमत्युग्रं वनवासकृतं पुरा॥१॥
verses.english: Markandeya said: O mighty-armed one, thus, in days of old Rama of unrivalled energy had experienced such a terrible disaster owing to his being exiled in the forests.
verses.bhavadeepa: जारूथ्यान् त्रिगुणदक्षिणानित्यर्जुनमिश्रः । जॄवॄभ्यामूथन्नित्युणादिसूत्रे जरूथं मांसमिति शाब्दिकाः । तदा मांसमयान् मांसादिदानप्रधानान् पुष्टानित्यर्थः । निरर्गलान् अन्नाद्यर्थिनामनावृतद्वारान् । जरूथोऽसुरविशेष इति वेदभाष्यम्। ‘जरूथं हन् यक्षि राये पुरन्धिम्’ इति मन्त्रवर्णात् । ‘जरूथं गरूथं गृणातेः’ इति यास्कवचनाच्च । जरूथं स्तोत्रम्। तथा चायं मन्त्रो निरुक्तभाष्ये व्याख्यातः - हेऽग्ने त्वां पुरन्धिं महान्तं समिधानः सम्यग्दीप्यन् वसिष्ठो मुनिः राये धनप्राप्तये जरूथं स्तोत्रं हन् गमयन् यक्षि जयति । अत्र जरतेः स्तुत्यर्थस्य शब्दसारूप्यादर्थाविरोधाच्च जरूथं स्तोत्रमित्युच्यत इति जारूथ्यान् स्तोत्रार्हानित्यर्थः ॥७०॥

verses.sanskrit: मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र क्षत्रियोऽसि परन्तप। बाहुवीर्याश्रिते मार्गे वर्तसे दीप्तनिर्णये॥२॥
verses.english: O most valiant of men, do not (therefore) lament (over your misfortune); for, O tormentor of foes, you are a Kshatriya. You are journeying along the path which calls forth the prowess of arms and which is calculated to lead to sure success.

verses.sanskrit: न हि ते वृजिनं किञ्चिद्वर्तते परमण्वपि। अस्मिन्मार्गे निषीदेयुः सेन्द्राऽपि ससुरासुराः॥३॥
verses.english: (By following this path) you have not incurred even an atom of sin. The gods together with Indra and the Asuras have (sometimes) to adopt this path.

verses.sanskrit: संहत्य निहतो वृत्रो मरुद्भिर्वज्रपाणिना। नमुचिश्चैव दुर्धर्षो दीर्घजिह्वा च राक्षसी॥४॥
verses.english: (It was by adopting this path) that the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra) together with the Marutas slew Vritra, the invincible Namuchi and the Rakshasa female Dirghajivha.

verses.sanskrit: सहायवति सर्वार्थाः सन्तिष्ठन्तीह सर्वशः। किं नु तस्याजितं सङ्ख्ये यस्य भ्राता धनञ्जयः॥५॥
verses.english: In this world, he, that is backed up, has all his desires gratified. What is there that cannot be overcome by him in battle whose brother is Dhananjaya?

verses.sanskrit: अयं च बलिनां श्रेष्ठो भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। युवानौ च महेष्वासौ वीरौ माद्रवती सुतौ॥६॥
verses.english: This Bhima of terrible prowess is the strongest of the strong; and the two youthful and heroic sons of Madravati are mighty bowmen.

verses.sanskrit: एभिः सहायैः कस्मात् त्वं विषीदसि परन्तप। य इमे वज्रिणः सेनां जयेयुः समरुद्गणाम्॥७॥
verses.english: Why, then, O tormentor of foes, do you grieve, since you have such supporters, as are capable of vanquishing the forces of the wielder of the thunderbolt together with the Marutas?

verses.sanskrit: त्वमप्येभिर्महेष्वासैः सहायैर्देवरूपिभिः। विजेष्यसि रणे सर्वानमित्रान् भरतर्षभ॥८॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharatas, with these mighty bowmen of celestials appearance you will surely conquer in battle all your enemies.

verses.sanskrit: इतश्च त्वमिमां पश्य सैन्धवेन दुरात्मना। बलिना वीर्यमत्तेन हृतामेभिर्महात्मभिः॥९॥
verses.english: Just see, these high-minded (brothers of yours) after achieving terrible feats (of arms) have rescued this daughter of Drupada carried off by the evil-minded Saindhava puffed up with pride and power. (And they) have also vanquished and reduced to subjection king Jayadratha.

verses.sanskrit: आनीतां द्रौपदीं कृष्णां कृत्त्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। जयद्रथं च राजानं विजितं वशमागतम्॥१०॥
असहायेन रामेण वैदेही पुनराहृता। हत्वा सङ्ख्ये दशग्रीवं राक्षसं भीमविक्रमम्॥११॥
verses.english: Again, the princess of Videha was rescued by Rama with almost no allies after having slain in battle the terribly-powerful ten-necked.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य शाखामृगा मित्राण्यृक्षाः कालमुखास्तथा। जात्यन्तरगता राजन्नेतद्बुद्ध्याऽनुचिन्तय॥१२॥
verses.english: Consider this, O king, by (the exercise of your) intelligence, that his (Rama's) only allies were the bears and the monkeys born in other orders of creation.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात् स त्वं कुरुश्रेष्ठ मा शुचो भरतर्षभ। त्वद्विधा हि महात्मानो न शोचन्ति परन्तप॥१३॥
verses.english: Therefore, O best of the Kurus, O most exalted of the Bharata, do not grieve over all this. O tormentor of foes, high-minded men like you never give way to sorrow.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमाश्वासितो राजा मार्कण्डेयेन धीमता। त्यक्त्वा दुःखमदीनात्मा पुनरप्येनमब्रवीत्॥१४॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Thus consoled by the intelligent Markandeya, the large-hearted king giving up his sorrow again spoke to Markandeya.
